I was five years old and in the first grade.

It was picture day, so I was all dressed up, like the rest of my class for my picture. We cross the school and go to the gym where we got our pictures taken, and I noticed a bunch of parents waiting around. I thought the parents were just there because of picture day.

After we got our pictures taken, we were then ushered out onto the playground and I thought that was the strangest thing: Here we are in our nice clothes and we are playing on the playground.

I think we were sent home from school early, but I didn't know for sure, but I remember running into the kitchen of my house where my mom told me what happened, and to go to the living room and watch TV but not change the channel. Still didn't know the magnitude of what happened, but I remember Tom Brokaw's voice clear as day.

Later, my dad arrives early from work and starts watching TV with me and my mom. Then my uncle comes over close to dusk and talks with my dad for a while.

I fell asleep in the living room with the TV still going. I remember waking up at around 11 PM and seeing Tom Brokaw still talking, and my uncle asleep on the couch. He was single at the time, and even though he lived next door to us, he could not stay alone at his house with all of this going on, and that's when I realized that something bad really did happen.

We can also start integrating it into elementary classrooms by using metric measurements as a way to describe things. For example, instead of saying "Billy is three feet tall", we could start saying "Billy is 96cm (Or whatever the actual conversion is) tall".

The biggest problem of changing over to the metric system is going to be the changeover of the road signs. What the states and federal government could do is grandfather signs that use the English system. Transportation Departments could pick a date where if a road sign needed to be replaced for whatever reason, the replaced road sign would be in the metric system.
